features.name: Expense Agent
features.description: New agent for processing employee expenses outside of traditional Business Central interface, supporting email, web app, and mobile inputs. Allows non-BC licensed users to submit expenses which are processed and stored in BC as backend. An AI-first agent that automates end-to-end expense management including receipt parsing, data extraction, itemization, and categorization.
features.status_evidence_quote: we are already in public preview. Uh we are in US only. More regions will come next month
caveats: Still in preview
May make AI mistakes
Feedback encouraged
Some manual steps still required like setting mileage information and posting
File size limit of 10 megabytes per expense
Batch limit of 25 files maximum, 50 megabytes total per batch
Shared email scenario limited to 100 emails per company
Each expense user limited to 50 expenses per company per day
Currently supports web and shared mailbox clients only, mobile coming later

features.name: Receipt Extraction via AI
features.description: Automatically extracts line items, vendor details, and financial information from receipts including PDFs, handwritten notes, and images in multiple languages.
caveats: AI may make mistakes
Requires user review
Itemization can be configured as required

features.name: Mileage Expense Calculation
features.description: Calculates mileage-based expenses for car travel with automatic route suggestion and mileage rate computation based on company configuration.
caveats: Route suggestions provided but user selectable

features.name: Per Diem Allowance Detection
features.description: Automatically detects trip duration and calculates per diem allowance from airline itineraries based on company configuration, extracting dates and destinations.
caveats: Requires itinerary format without pricing

features.name: Multi-Language Receipt Processing
features.description: Processes receipts with handwritten notes and documents in multiple languages including Vietnamese and other Asian languages automatically.

features.name: Currency Conversion
features.description: Automatically converts expense amounts to the company's base currency, handling multiple currencies in a single expense report.

features.name: Mobile Expense Submission
features.description: Mobile app for expense submission featuring camera capture, share-to-app functionality, and feed-based UI similar to social media for viewing incoming expenses.
caveats: Scanning quality depends on lighting
Feed experience may come to web app

features.name: Web App for Expense Entry
features.description: Dedicated web-based experience for submitting and managing expenses with drag-and-drop, copy-paste, and upload capabilities.
caveats: Feed experience may be added later

features.name: Approval Workflow
features.description: Managers review submitted expense reports via web interface and email notification, with ability to approve, request changes, or send back for revision.

features.name: Policy and Rules Engine
features.description: Runs company policies and rules on expenses to ensure compliance with finance department requirements and company settings.

features.name: Receipt Confirmation UI
features.description: Mobile and web interface allowing users to swipe or confirm receipt data before submitting for approval, with option to edit or defer problematic entries.

features.name: Speedboat Team Methodology
features.description: A self-contained team structure empowered to make rapid decisions, operate like a startup, and iterate quickly without traditional organizational constraints while keeping data integration with Business Central.
caveats: Still subject to organizational realities

features.name: AI-First Development Approach
features.description: Using AI and LLM models as much as possible, leveraging GitHub Copilot and other AI tools throughout the development process instead of manual coding.
caveats: Models have improved significantly; Opus 4.5 was breakthrough

features.name: Agentic Development with Code Generation
features.description: 99 percent plus of the expense agent code is generated; developers use CLI tools and GitHub Copilot to generate code artifacts including skills, agents files, and instructions.
caveats: Human developer control still maintained
100% automation not pursued

features.name: Unified Repository Architecture
features.description: All system components including mobile experiences, web experiences, backends, and Business Central integration are stored in a single GitHub repository to enable AI cross-stack coordination.
caveats: New tools emerging that can coordinate across repos

features.name: Model-First LLM Approach
features.description: Using LLM models to feed images, PDFs and data for extraction, categorization, validation, and policy validation from written policies.
caveats: Policy validation from written policies not yet complete

features.name: Offline Evaluation Methodology
features.description: Evaluation based on curated datasets with ground truth labeling, using metrics including accuracy requirements to measure LLM quality on receipt processing tasks.
caveats: Requires 95% accuracy for production
Requires manual labeling effort

features.name: Online Evaluation with LLM Judge
features.description: Production evaluation run on real data using another LLM as a judge to validate extracted data quality.

features.name: Receipt Data Extraction and Categorization
features.description: Agent extracts data from receipts, performs itemization for specific categories, applies categorization (airline, hotel, etc.), and validates data matching.

features.name: Dataset Preparation with Ground Truth Labeling
features.description: 1,500 manually labeled datasets created with ground truth labels for receipt data including merchant, amount, category, currency, and date for training and evaluation.
caveats: Significant manual effort required

features.name: Synthetic Data Generation for Edge Cases
features.description: Synthetic datasets generated by LLM for both invoices and ground truth to capture corner cases not present in real receipts, identified through analysis and added as new test cases.
caveats: Synthetic data may not perfectly represent all real-world scenarios

features.name: Automated Quality Pipeline
features.description: An automatic pipeline that runs data sets, applies quality metrics and accuracy heuristics to evaluate Expense Agent extraction results. The pipeline compares model output against ground truth using non-deterministic comparison with applied metrics.

features.name: 95 Percent Accuracy Requirement
features.description: Microsoft requires a 95% accuracy threshold for shipping products. The Expense Agent started at 65% accuracy and needed improvement to meet the shipping requirement.

features.name: Hill Climbing Loop
features.description: An iterative improvement process that uses pipeline results to progressively improve model accuracy. Process involves fixing data set issues, improving prompts, and creating synthetic data sets to catch corner cases.

features.name: Model Comparison Framework
features.description: Automated comparison of different language models (Anthropic, Claude, GPT variations) on the same evaluation pipeline. Shows model performance differences across specific tasks like currency extraction, date extraction, and other fields.
caveats: Comparison results depend on specific region availability and pricing

features.name: Harmful Eval Testing and Red Teaming
features.description: Security-focused evaluation methodology using red teaming tools to produce test invoices with harmful content. Tests model resistance to producing unlawful or policy-violating outputs, addressing hate, unfairness, sexual harm and related issues.
caveats: Harmful eval testing has input but not necessarily output; desired output is for LLM to refuse generation

features.name: Online Evals in Production
features.description: Real-world evaluation running on production data with receipts from actual Expense Agent users. Uses LLM-as-judge methodology with another model validating against original input. Sends telemetry signals (no raw data) for mismatch scenarios to enable continuous hill climbing.
caveats: No raw data emitted to telemetry, only privacy-preserving signals
Relies on LLM-as-judge which may not be perfect

features.name: Eval-Driven Development
features.description: Development methodology where evaluation comes first, similar to test-driven development. Process involves starting with evals and then writing code. Includes both offline and online eval types to enable model comparison and continuous hill climbing for accuracy improvement.

features.name: Expense Agent Architecture
features.description: A global service architecture where Expense Agent sits outside BC as a special agent. Serves both agentic and non-agentic clients, parsing receipts and passing data to ERP systems. Code generation was nearly 100% agentic, but architecture was compliance and people-driven.
caveats: Architecture is compliance-driven due to Microsoft security and privacy requirements
Uses Azure stack exclusively

features.name: Azure Front Door Entry Point
features.description: Azure Front Door serves as the main entry point for the Expense Agent public global service. Required by Microsoft for public facing services, providing out-of-the-box reliability, design features, and multiple infrastructure capabilities.
caveats: Mandatory for all public Microsoft services

features.name: Gateway Component
features.description: Python-based App Service component that sits after Azure Front Door in the Expense Agent service architecture. Lightweight stateless pass-through component handling critical authorization and authentication functions.

features.name: Global Service Instances
features.description: Multiple Expense Agent service instances deployed globally working together with Azure Front Door to provide automatic routing and proximity to clients in different regions.

features.name: Authorization and Authentication Flow
features.description: The expense agent uses tenant ID and user email claims to authenticate users and locate their Business Central environment through a broadcasting mechanism with Redis caching to optimize repeated lookups.
caveats: Broadcasting mechanism can stress the system if not cached efficiently
Uses Redis cache to avoid repeated broadcasts

features.name: Azure Architecture Components
features.description: The expense agent is built on Azure infrastructure with Azure Front Door as entry point, a Python-based gateway component for authentication and authorization, and Azure Functions-based processors for expense parsing and orchestration.
caveats: Requires Azure resources across multiple regions for global service
Uses durable entities for orchestration

features.name: Expense Management Module
features.description: A new Business Central functionality providing expense management capabilities independent of the agent. It includes features for managing expenses, though less automated than when used with the expense agent.
caveats: Has fewer functionalities when used without the expense agent
Expense agent recommended for full functionality

features.name: Expense Users Entity
features.description: A new Business Central entity that allows creation of expense users attached to employees. These users do not require a Business Central license and can submit expenses via web app, mobile app, or shared mailbox. Can be bulk imported from existing employees or from organizational directory via Graph API.
caveats: Do not require Business Central licenses
Must be created before users can submit expenses

features.name: Shared Mailbox Integration
features.description: Expense users can submit expenses through a shared mailbox where all submission emails are registered in the system. This is one of the supported submission channels alongside the web app.
caveats: Limited to 100 emails per company in shared email scenario

features.name: Mobile Client Support
features.description: Mobile app support for the expense agent is coming soon, allowing users to submit expenses from mobile devices in addition to web and shared mailbox options.
caveats: Not yet available at time of presentation

features.name: Import Existing Employees as Expense Users
features.description: Action to import all existing employees into the system as expense users with a single button press, using graph API to pull all registered organization members with correct information.

features.name: Welcome Email for Expense Users
features.description: Automated welcome email sent to expense users containing instructions on how to use the expense agent, links to access the web app, email submission details, and other getting started information.

features.name: Expense User Approver Configuration
features.description: Ability to designate expense users as approvers and configure which other users they can approve expenses for. Supports both manual per-user setup and default approver configuration at the system level.

features.name: Default Configurations for Agent Activation
features.description: Option to auto-create default configurations including number series, payment methods, employee posting groups, and expense posting groups on first agent activation. Only needs to be configured once.

features.name: Expense Categories with Descriptions
features.description: Configurable expense categories where detailed descriptions act as prompts for the agent to correctly categorize expenses. Each category can have default payment type, refundability settings, and required additional information like itemization or participants.
caveats: Agent accuracy depends on category description quality

features.name: Expense Subcategories
features.description: Sub-level categorization within main expense categories, also using descriptions as prompts for agent itemization. Allows fine-grained control such as marking specific line items as non-refundable while the overall category is refundable.

features.name: Per Diem and Location Configuration
features.description: Location-based per diem calculation that allows different configurations by state rather than country. Supports regional variations such as different per diem rates between New York and New Jersey.

features.name: Expense Rules Configuration
features.description: Hard rules based on logical and mathematical conditions such as minimum/maximum amounts, requiring justification above certain thresholds, and controlling which categories require specific information like participants.

features.name: Expense Policies
features.description: Natural language policies that allow specification of scenarios such as when business class can be booked, four-star hotel eligibility, or when alcohol can be expensed based on context like team events versus personal dinners.
features.status_evidence_quote: we are working for the policies as well uh which will come uh pretty soon
caveats: Not yet available; currently at policy document stage

features.name: Expense Report Open Notification
features.description: Configurable reminder feature that notifies expense users when they have open reports requiring attention. Notifications can be sent at configurable intervals to help users remember to upload and complete reports.

features.name: Mileage Expense Configuration
features.description: Configurable settings for mileage expense calculation and per diem configuration within the simplified expense agent setup dialog.

features.name: Expense Agent Consumption Tracking
features.description: Admin page showing billing overview including different actions taken on specific reports, co-pilot credits used, and overall usage metrics for the expense agent.

features.name: Expense Agent KPIs
features.description: Key performance indicator display showing metrics including emails processed via email attachment, expenses created, reports created, and calculated time savings based on telemetry.

features.name: Expense Report View and Adjustment
features.description: Finance operator page allowing viewing all expense reports across the organization, opening individual reports to see all lines and attachments submitted by each expense user, and making manual adjustments to line items.

features.name: Intelligent Reimbursement Classification
features.description: Agent logic that determines reimbursement amounts based on payment method - reimburses cash payments but not company card payments.

features.name: Refundable Classification Tab
features.description: Tab in expense lines showing which expenses are categorized as refundable and which are not.

features.name: Billable Expense Line Marking
features.description: Feature allowing administrators to mark individual expense lines as billable to specific customers.

features.name: Project Attachment to Expenses
features.description: Ability to attach projects to individual expense lines or full reports for cost allocation.
caveats: Currently only available from desktop, web app version is work in progress

features.name: Expense Posting Workflow
features.description: Posting flow where approved expense reports are converted to GL entries and familiar Business Central posting mechanics.

features.name: Expense-Level Feedback with Thumbnails
features.description: Thumbs up/down feedback mechanism at individual expense level with optional screenshot capture and privacy controls for issue reporting.
caveats: Screenshot capture available but users can hide personal information

features.name: Generic Feature Feedback Mechanism
features.description: Feedback channel for suggesting missing features or general product improvement requests.
